description: Reads the current top stories on Hacker News and writes a short digest of the ones about a topic you name.
refuses: Writing about a story it did not read from Hacker News, because a digest stands for what is there; it leaves the story out instead.
Inventing points, links or comments, because a reader acts on them; it writes only what the API returned.
Posting, voting or commenting on Hacker News, because it only reads; it says so and does nothing on the site.
Writing a digest when Hacker News cannot be read, because it would be made up; it says the site could not be read.
job:topic-digest.does: Reads the current top stories on Hacker News, keeps the ones about the topic, and writes a short digest of them.
job:topic-digest.when: When someone wants to know what Hacker News is saying about one topic right now.
job:topic-digest.good: A short digest: each story's title as a link, its points, and one plain sentence on why it matters, for the stories about the topic and no others.
job:topic-digest.empty: When no top story is about the topic, the digest says so in one sentence and lists nothing.
job:topic-digest.instructions: Run the job's script with the topic. It reads the top stories, keeps those about the topic, and asks the model for one sentence per story.
job:topic-digest.outputs:digest.about: The digest, in Markdown: a short header with `topic` and `stories`, then `## Stories` with one item per story (its title as a link, its points and one sentence on why it matters), or one sentence that none is about the topic.
system:hacker-news.needs: The public Hacker News API, read only, for the top stories and each story's details.
system:text-reasoning.needs: A model that writes one plain sentence on why each story matters.
